Prime Minister Narendra Modi today spoke to brave Indian pilot. Captain Smith Machar,
whose heroics in thwarting of an attack were his co-pilot, saved 180 lives on the fly-through-by-flight
from the way to Tel Aviv. Captain Machar gave details of his experience to the Prime Minister
and spoke of what gave him courage during the incident. The Prime Minister applauded
his bravery and wished him a quick recovery, Mr Modi said the whole country is praying for
him.
He said Captain Smith's courage, presence of mind and composure saved many lives.
The Prime Minister lauded Smith's spirit, saying that the country can proudly say that
Indians are not those who take lives but those who are willing to risk their lives
to save others.
During the interaction, an emotional Smith shared that PM Modi is his biggest idol and expressed
how special and proud he felt to receive the call.
We are fighting for our lives and our lives.
At that time, you didn't care about your own life,
you didn't care about the lives of everyone else.
And the biggest thing is that you have increased your pride
of 144 crores of people.
And that's why I am proud of Raza.
I would like to hear from you.
Sir, for me, I was saying that
I can take the first act of my life.
The co-pilot accused of assaulting Captain Smith Machar has been transferred to Abu Dhabi,
the Saudi Press Agency, SBA quoting an official source at the Saudi Ministry of Interior reported
that both pilots left the country for Abu Dhabi after receiving medical clearance.
The Indian Embassy in Abu Dhabi had yesterday informed that Captain Machar had been brought
to the UAE and was recovering well.
The nation is paying homage to the father of the nation, Mahatma Gandhi, on his 157th
birth anniversary today.
A servidharma prarthana sabha was held at Bapu Samadhi in Rajkhat in the national capital.
President Robert E. Murmur attended the servidharma prarthana this morning and paid floral
tributes to the father of the nation.
Vice President Sipiratha Krishnan, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Lok Sabha Speaker
Om Birla, Union Housing and Urban Affairs Minister Manohar Lal, and Delhi Chief
Chief Minister Ekha Gupta also paid tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajkhat.
The nation is also paying homage to former Prime Minister Al Bahadur Shastri on his 122nd
birth anniversary today.
He was born on the 2nd of October 1904 in Pandit Deen Dayalupadhyay Nagar, previously
known as Mughal Sarai, in Uttar Pradesh.
As a teenager, he joined India's freedom struggle and participated in the non-cooperation
movement in 1921.
Following independence, Shastriji held several important positions in Uttar Pradesh and later
in the Union government.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid floral tribute to the former Prime Minister at his memorial,
Vijaykart in the national capital this morning.
Several Indian diplomatic missions across the world today marked Mahatma Gandhi's
birth anniversary by paying floral tributes and recalling his timeless ideals of truth,
both non-violence and peace. Marking Gandhi gently on the International Day of Non-Violence,
the Indian High Commission in Australia offered floral tribute at the Mahatma Gandhi Statue
at Leib Park in Canberra.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of Jan Seva, Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues
guided by this vision. For Seva and Sushasan, the government has been ceaselessly working
towards achieving Vixit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment,
this dedication is transforming lives. Today in our special series, we bring you an instance
of how this vision has been translated into action through Atal Tunnel.
The Atal Tunnel constructed beneath the world-famous Rohtang Pass under extremely challenging
geographical conditions is a remarkable example of modern engineering and the technical
expertise of the border roads organization.
One of the country's important infrastructure and strategic projects, the Airtel Tunnel provides
all-weather year-round connectivity between Kullu and the tribal district of Lahalspiti
in Himachal Pradesh.
It has also emerged as an important landmark for development, tourism, and strategic connectivity
in the state.
Situated at an altitude of around 10,000 feet above sea level and extending for
more than 9 kilometers, the Airtel Tunnel was inaugurated by the honorable Prime
Minister Narendra Modi on the 3rd of October 2020. The project was constructed at a cost
of around 3,200 crore rupees. The tunnel has brought significant positive changes to the
lives of people in the region. Sonam Jangpo, a resident of Kailang district headquarters
of Lahalspiti, says the tunnel has improved access to essential services such as transport,
healthcare and education. He expressed his gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi
for this historic gift to the region.
My name is Sonam Jangpo and I am a resident of Kelong.
Before the utter tunnel was opened, we had to travel to Kullu Manali via the Rohtang Pass
which caused us a lot of difficulties.
After the tunnel was opened, access to healthcare facilities has also become much easier.
In case of an emergency, we can now reach Kullu within just one or two hours.
It has also brought great convenience to our farmers and horticultures.
Our vegetables can now reach the market on the same day.
The project has also received a major boost.
We sincerely thank the central government because we are now connected with the rest
of the country throughout the year.
We also express our gratitude to our Honorable Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi.
The utter tunnel has not only given a major boost to tourism in Himachal Pradesh but
has also made year-round connectivity to the border areas, particularly Leh-Ladak,
more convenient, Ritesh Kapoor, Akashwani News, Shimla.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his 138th episode of Man ki Baat program appreciated hockey
Olympian from Punjab, Rajinder Singh's senior for his efforts to discover and coach sports
talent from the villages of the state, lauding him for pursuing his passion through the
round-glass hockey academy to train children in hockey in villages.
The Prime Minister said Rajinder has a very clear focus in identifying children who lack
access to excellent coaching facilities at village level. More from our correspondent.
Olympian Rajendra Singh was part of the gold medal-winning Indian hockey team at the 1980
Olympics. He played his last international match in 1982 champion's trophy, which India
won from Pakistan and got a bronze medal, with him converting three penalty corners
into goals. He joined Sports Authority of India in 1990 and status his coaching career
during his tenure, sub-junior and junior hockey teams achieved many national awards
after his retirement from SAI.
This Dronacharya awardee joined Round Glass Sports Academy in 2020 and started nurturing
the young tail end from villages to make them national level players.
I was stunned to hear Honorable Prime Minister Narendra Maudhiji talk about me, Rajinder
Singh Olympic gold medalist, Arjuna Wadi and as a coach, Dronacharya Wadi in his
monkey bath.
It is a very proud moment not only for me but my all fellow
leagues, Olympians, international players in India.
You're sure to continue coaching the young talent to build strong hockey team for India.
Rajesh Bali, Akash Vani News, Jalandhar.

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal held bilateral meetings with his counterparts
from France, Canada, Saudi Arabia and South Korea on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Minister's
meeting in Milwaukee in the United States.
The discussions focused on strengthening bilateral trade relations with the respective countries
during his meeting with France's Minister of Delegate for Foreign Trade and Economic
Attractiveness, Nicolas Forissier.
Goyal discussed ways to expand trade and investment ties expedite the
India-EU free trade agreement and deepen cooperation in areas including aerospace
manufacturing, UPI integration and joint innovation initiatives. Mr Goyal also
held a productive meeting with Canadian International Trade Minister Manindar
Sidhu. The two ministers reviewed ongoing negotiations for the India-Canada
comprehensive economic partnership agreement and reaffirmed their
commitment to expediting the talks. The agreement launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in March aims to take bilateral trade between the two
countries to 50 billion US dollars by 2030. The United Nations has welcomed India's approval
of the 1.86 lakh crore rupee Green Energy Corridor phase 3, describing the grid strengthening
and battery storage scheme as a major step that will deliver big dividends for the
countries, people and economy.
In a statement to a news agency, UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Steele said
the initiative would help India harness its growing renewable energy capacity, meet rising
electricity needs and further strengthen its position as a global leader in solar energy.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has said Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has very
good ideas aimed at finding a mutually acceptable solution to the Ukraine conflict.
Speaking at the Valdai Forum, Mr. Puthin noted that Mr. Modi regularly raises the topic of
ending the war during their discussions and shows strong interest in a peaceful settlement.
Mr. Puthin described India's diplomatic position as neutral yet deeply invested in bringing
the hostilities to an end, while Mr. Modi has previously emphasised that India stands
firmly on the side of peace. Mr. Puthin expressed gratitude for Mr. Modi's persistent engagement
development, and practical approach towards dialogue and diplomacy.
Indian athletes continued their strong performance of the ongoing Asian Games in Aichi, Nagoya,
Japan, winning several medals across multiple sporting events today.
In boxing, Lovlina Aborghain clinched a historic gold medal in the women's 75kg category,
defeating China's Pao Ziyi by a unanimous 5-0 decision in the final.
It is only in the second gold medal in women's boxing at the Asian Games following Mary Combs Gold in 2014.
Earlier in the women's recovery archery team created history by winning its made in Asian Games gold medal.
The trio of Ankita Bhakat, Katie Sharma and Kumkum Mahod defeated world champion South Korea 5-3 in a thrilling final.
India also secured a silver medal in the mixed recovery team archery event.
the Indian duo of Kumkumohod and Dheeraj Bhamadevra finished runners-up after losing 3-5 to China
in a closely contested final. In sailing they recommended one the bronze medal in the women's
dinghy event, the 29-year-old Indian sailor finished third with overall 14 points. With
these performances, India climbed to sixth position in the overall medal standings.
The country's medal tally rose to 72 medals, comprising 12 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze.

The Met Department said thunderstorms and lightning conditions will continue over
